source_evidence: Each ADR represents one or more shares of foreign stock or a fraction of a share.
answer: An American Depositary Receipt (ADR) is a way to own a financial instrument representing shares in a non-U.S. company. One ADR can represent one or more shares, or part of a share. Its price corresponds to the stock’s price in the company’s home market, adjusted for how many ADRs represent the company’s shares. U.S. investors can purchase ADRs that trade in the United States through a U.S. broker. Owning an ADR gives the investor the right to obtain the stock it represents, though investors usually find it more convenient to own the ADR.
